_comment: Macro benchmark baseline: four bots replaying the standard session.
Regenerate: bot bench --rounds 360 --json benches/macro-baseline.json
Gate: CI fails if p99 exceeds 2x this value, or 5% of a tick, whichever
is larger (bot::bench::REGRESSION_FACTOR and NOISE_FLOOR_US), or if the
workload moved (bot::bench::TICK_DRIFT).
REBASELINED 2026-08-24, and the reason is the SAME one as both previous
times: the workload moved, not the server. `09becc7` made a block come
apart sub-node by sub-node over its break time, so a dig that used to
finish in about a tick now occupies fifteen - and the standard session is
mostly digging. 626 ticks became ~8,700 at identical parameters. p99 went
from the seventh-worst tick of 626 to the eighty-seventh of 8,700, which
is a different statistic about a different distribution.
`TICK_DRIFT` is new and exists so this is never diagnosed by hand again.
The old workload check compared bots and rounds - what a person changes on
purpose - and both incidents changed how long a ROUND TAKES while leaving
the parameters alone. The gate now says `workload moved: the baseline ran
626 ticks and this run ran 8854` instead of naming a regression nobody can
find. Six red nights across two incidents bought that one line.
THE NUMBERS BELOW COME FROM A CI RUNNER, WHICH IS THE CHANGE THAT MATTERS.
Every previous baseline was recorded on the reference workstation and then
used to gate a run on shared cloud silicon, and `NOISE_FLOOR_US` existed
purely to paper over the difference. On the old workload the runner was
1.65x this workstation; on this one its TAIL is five times as slow, because
the session is now dominated by sub-node edits and relighting rather than
by the join burst. Gating a 3.3 ms measurement against a 0.66 ms baseline
is comparing processors. So the baseline is the runner's own, the ratio
does the work again, and the floor goes back to being a backstop.
Source: nightly run at af40f31, 2026-08-24 - 8854 ticks, p99 3338 us. The
run two nights earlier read 3109 us over 9109 ticks, so the runner's p99 on
this workload is stable to within about 7 percent, which the previous
workload's p99 never was (578, 707, 1027, 1366, 1612 over five runs).
The reference workstation reads far lower and that is expected: a run
faster than the baseline is never a failure. Five runs there on this
workload gave 636, 675, 644, 687 and 636 us over 8647-8703 ticks - note
how TIGHT that is compared with the old workload's spread. The longer
session moved p99 out of the join burst and into the body of the
distribution, which is what made it a statistic worth gating on.
_machine: GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest runner, release build
_reference_machine: dev container, AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D: p99 660 us (median of five)
